reason: Not refuted as a zero-cost, read-only calibration procedure. It creates no mechanism, uses no kernel, slot or runtime, and cannot change any score, so R1-R10 and R8 do not apply. Its value is calibration and lessons only; the expected score gain is 0. Four parts of the procedure are wrong or stale and must be amended before it is recorded. (a) STALE FINALS PREMISE: at 20:33 UTC (commit 620f718) the user changed the finals to one aimed at public and one aimed at private (default private = #37), lifted R7, and allowed K2 public probes (3 slots tonight, then 5 a day). The finals may therefore no longer be #37 + #38, and step (3)'s check 'team Score = max(k37, k38)/1000' and the fixed list of five refs are stale. (b) PAGINATION: kaggle 2.2.4 KaggleApi.competition_submissions and the CLI both default to page_size=20. The CLI -v prints about 29 or more rows today, but with up to ~18 new probes #34 would sit around row 23. The procedure must pass page_size=100 and fail loudly on any missing ref. (c) RATE LIMIT: poll.log at 20:36:50Z shows three 429 Too Many Requests errors on ListSubmissions, so the hourly read needs retry and backoff. The claim that poll.log keeps 60 lines is loose (the cap is 60 lines per poll), but the advice to call the CLI directly is right. (d) BOARD CHECK: 'our Score = max/1000' cannot tell the boards apart when the private max shows the same value as our public score (e.g. 0.954 on both). Diffing against the saved 23:30Z public snapshot can tell them apart. The medal lines (gold 10 + 0.2%, silver 5%, bronze 10%, about 17/197/395 at N ~3,950) are correct. The timer is feasible but session-only: CronCreate one-shots fire only while the REPL is idle and die with the session, and the cron is in local time UTC+3.
fix: Record as a dated CONTEXT procedure line with these amendments. (1) 29 Sep after the 20:00 UTC tick: save the API SELECTED refs and read the finals set F from them, not a hard-coded #37/#38. The read list = #34 56545267, #35 56545786, P36 56555189, #37 56563521, #38 56563534, plus every probe submitted from 26 Sep 20:33 UTC on (all submissions get private scores). (2) 29 Sep ~23:00-23:45 UTC: `python -m kaggle competitions leaderboard biohub-cell-tracking-during-development -d -p experiments/private_read/`, renamed with a timestamp, plus a submissions CSV. Retry up to 3 times with 60-120 s backoff on 429. Timer: a one-shot CronCreate at local '27 2 30 9 *' (= 29 Sep 23:27 UTC), or set it from the 18ff4796 tick at 29 Sep 17:57 UTC. Both are session-bound, so note in CONTEXT that the user reads manually if the session is gone. (3) From 30 Sep 00:15 UTC, hourly with backoff: KaggleApi().competition_submissions(comp, page_size=100) -> private_score. Fail loudly if any listed ref is missing. Cross-check with `kaggle competitions submissions ... -v --page-size 100` called directly. Log `date -u` at first sight. (4) Board check: the downloaded CSV counts as the PRIVATE board only if (i) our Score = max over F of the private displays AND (ii) its top-50 order/scores differ from the 23:30Z public snapshot. Otherwise use the Private tab in the browser, read-only. (5)-(7) as proposed: medal lines from N, C1-C5 and I in thousandths, both reads (first publication and after cleanup), LESSONS s5 and CONTEXT section 11. Also add the finals-change caveat: if F != {#37, #38}, the team result is max over F, and the rank-forecast read (R12P-3) must be redone for that pair.
realistic_gain: 0 on score (post-deadline, read-only). Value is calibration only: clean private contrasts C2/C3 and a rank-vs-forecast read for LESSONS and future competitions. Without the amendments the procedure could misread the board, miss refs because of the 20-row default page, or check against stale finals.
